newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slide with metals at opening.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slide with metals at opening.

text.p: Australian shares followed metals prices down at the open on Tuesday, breaking a five day winning streak with gold and base metals miners suffering most.
Turnover, though, remained at only moderate levels.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 14.8 points to 2275.6.
Brokers said with buying support dissipating as expiries finished, a slide in metals prices had exacerbated the fall.
"Golds and metals are the ones to watch. They have taken the worst hits with the rest only a little weaker," said a dealer at a Sydney-based broker.
The gold index underlined his point, dropping 2.5 percent early after the gold price fell through support at the US$380 level in offshore markets.
The dealer said recent options and futures expiries had buoyed buying interest in the majors in the last few days and some selling now was not a surprise.
"The support of the last few days is not there so some selling is not a shock," he said.

Corporate wise, Australia's biggest retailer reported a 33.8 percent lower net profit of A$280.4 million for the year to July 28. Its shares lost were just a cent lower at A$4.58 in a slightly weaker industrials sector.
WMC shares suffered most among the leading miners, its shares losing 23 cents to A$7.90 while the golds were lower across the board.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about four to one, while about 37 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
